blocks.text: A capacitor is a device that can store electrical energy in the form of an electric field. Two such devices are discussed here: isolated spherical conductors and parallel-plate capacitors (16.5).
A spherical conductor far from other conductors or influences is an isolated spherical conductor. Its ability to store electric charge is called its capacitance, C.

blocks.title: Capacitance of an isolated sphere
blocks.text: The capacitance of an isolated spherical conductor is the charge stored on the sphere per unit electric potential at its surface: C = Q/V (16.25). The SI unit is the farad (F): 1 F is the capacitance of a sphere that stores 1 coulomb when its potential is 1 volt (1 F = 1 C / 1 V).

blocks.alt: Left: charge Q is brought along a dashed path from far away to point A, and charge q from far away to point B, a distance r from A; steps: bringing Q needs no work, bringing q needs W = qV = kQq/r; Ep = (1/4 pi eo) Qq / r. Right: an isolated sphere of radius R with positive charges spread over its surface; C = Q/V, V = (1/4 pi eo) Q/R, C = 4 pi eo R, and 4 pi eo er R in a medium.
blocks.caption: Potential energy of two charges, and an isolated sphere (original diagram after Figs 16.4 and 16.5).
blocks.long_description: The first charge costs nothing to place; the second must be pushed into the first charge's potential. That work is the stored energy of the pair.

blocks.text: The potential at the surface of a sphere of radius R carrying charge Q is V = (1/4 pi eo) Q / R. Substituting in C = Q/V gives C = 4 pi eo R (16.26). In a medium of dielectric constant er, C = 4 pi eo er R (16.27). So the capacitance of a spherical conductor does not depend on the charge or the potential; it depends only on the radius and the medium. A larger sphere stores more charge at the same surface potential, and a dielectric medium increases the capacitance.

Find the capacitance of an isolated metal sphere of radius 10 cm in air. Solution: C = 4 pi eo R = 4 x 3.14 x (8.85 x 10^-12 F m^-1)(0.10 m) = 1.1 x 10^-11 F = 11 pF. Even the whole Earth (R = 6.4 x 10^6 m) has a capacitance of only about 7 x 10^-4 F, which shows that one farad is a very large unit.

blocks.prompt: Two isolated spheres have radii 5 cm and 10 cm. Which has the greater capacitance, and by what factor?
blocks.explanation: The 10 cm sphere, twice as large, because C = 4 pi eo R is proportional to R.

items: A capacitor stores energy in an electric field.
Isolated sphere: C = Q/V = 4 pi eo R (4 pi eo er R in a medium).
1 F = 1 C/V, a very large unit.
